summary: The note describes how Brooksville passed a municipal campaign finance reform ordinance, signed by Mayor Elena Martinez on September 3, 2023, after a grassroots coalition responded to heavy spending in the 2022 mayoral race. The reform created public campaign funding, faster disclosure rules and lower contribution caps, taking effect January 1, 2024. In the April 12, 2024 spring council elections it opened the field to newcomers and raised youth turnout to 55%, and similar movements are reported in neighboring cities.
one_line: Brooksville's 2023 campaign finance reform created public funding and tighter disclosure, boosting newcomers and youth turnout in the 2024 council elections and inspiring other cities.
key_facts: Mayor Elena Martinez signed Brooksville's campaign finance reform ordinance at town hall on September 3, 2023.
The 2022 mayoral race in Brooksville saw unprecedented expenditures that dwarfed what average citizens could afford, fueling the reform push.
Voices for a Vibrant Brooksville was an activist group that spearheaded the reform campaign.
Dr. Marcus Yee, a political science lecturer at Brooksville University, warned on October 10, 2023 that a few deep-pocketed donors can disproportionately influence an election.
The Brooksville Campaign Finance Reform Act created a public campaign finance system, with candidates qualifying for public funding by showing a threshold of small-donor support.
Campaign contributions over $100 must be reported within 24 hours, with donors' identities published in a public database.
The cap on individual contributions was halved; campaign strategist Aaron Leigh called it "a seismic shift empowering the many over the few."
The referendum on campaign finance reform was scheduled to coincide with the November 2023 local elections.
The new framework took effect on January 1, 2024, ahead of the spring council elections.
Hector Gonzalez, a 26-year-old community worker, launched a credible campaign thanks to the reforms, using door-to-door canvassing and social media.
Incumbent finance chair Roberta Jackson, age forty, was among the seasoned council members facing unexpected challenges.
In the April 12, 2024 spring council elections, turnout among 18- to 25-year-olds reached a historic 55%.
Wagner Consulting, founded by Michael Wagner, set up workshops to help candidates use the public funding model.
Neighboring cities reportedly have similar reform movements gaining traction after Brooksville's example.
